description: A distortion built from a peaking filter with a saturating feedback path, wrapped in a delay-free loop; what its four knobs mean is decided by the mode knob below them

params.text: Sets the frequency of the peaking filter, 5Hz to 1000Hz, in every mode
In mode 0 it sets the filter's Q and cuts the drive as it rises; in mode 1 it raises the drive and the feedback together; in mode 2 it raises the feedback drive and the feedback together
In mode 0 it sweeps the filter gain from -24dB to 24dB and raises the feedback; in mode 1 it sweeps the gain from -14dB to 14dB and lowers the Q; in mode 2 it only lowers the Q
In modes 0 and 1 it sets how hard the feedback path saturates; in mode 2 it sets the filter's own drive and lifts the gain from 0dB to 24dB
Chooses which of three mappings the four knobs above use, 0, 1 or 2; the number is printed under the knob, and changing it fades the output down and back so the switch is not heard as a click

outputs.text: The distorted audio, at ten times the filter's own output

notes: the three mappings are the maker's own designs, the second by Isabel Kaspriskie. They are not more and less of one thing, so a setting found in one mode has no counterpart in another.
the filter runs at twice the sample rate when the module is added; the oversampling menu changes that.
menu: Oversampling: 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x — sets how many times the internal sample rate is raised before the nonlinearity is computed; higher settings reduce aliasing and cost more CPU

inputs.0:
bipolar · continuous · one channel only
